hardware.core_cpu_cuda_tests: pc33 NVIDIA H20-3e; CPU tests use the same source tree

implementation.auto_resolution: compact/evict only for supported TLI Qwen3 with fixed near geometry and compact-compatible ordinary shared-head two-level selection; otherwise auto resolves to legacy/retain. Explicit compact remains fail-closed.
implementation.direct_lifecycle: prepare_direct_prefill -> one-shot B=1 unpadded dense prefill -> finalize_direct_prefill -> capture/decode
implementation.dense_prefill_semantics: staging update writes linear/ring partitions and returns the original complete K/V to dense attention
implementation.skip_finalize: 13 skip layers retain fixed sink plus cyclic Near/SWA ring and release linear Sink/Far staging
implementation.non_skip_finalize: 23 non-skip layers retain full linear storage for existing L1/L2 and gather kernels
implementation.known_non_skip_optimization: ring elision avoids the previously measured 0.592 GiB redundant staging peak

core_tests.note: The nine CUDA tests skipped by the earlier CPU-only run executed in this final run.

gpu_functional_gates.environment_note: The trailing pc02 pytest invocation failed because neither remote Python had pytest; it is not counted as a test pass. The small-model CUDA tests passed in the pc33 core run.

eager_cross_check.attribution: The identical 32K/128K graph-vs-eager differences occur in the conversion arm too, while direct-eager and conversion-eager are exactly equal. This is a shared decode numerical-path limitation, not a direct-prefill regression; strict cross-mode bit-exactness is therefore not claimed.

hybrid.ragged_lengths: B2 uses 16384/20000; B8 uses 16384..23552 in 1024-token steps; B32 uses 32 rows of 16384

ruler_small_sample.scope: Byte-identical direct/conversion outputs on these 16 examples only; not a full RULER quality claim.

memory_no_skip_gib.measurement: torch.cuda.memory_allocated/max_memory_allocated and per-layer numel*element_size; capacity formulas and reserved memory are not substitutes
memory_no_skip_gib.interpretation: Direct prefill does not reduce steady main KV when every layer is non-skip. Its measured peak benefit is avoiding the old DynamicCache duplicate on subsequent requests; first-request peaks differ by only about 0.02 GiB.

memory_static_skip.first_peak_attribution: The skip arm's first-request direct peak is 0.21-0.24 GiB higher. The independent 13-layer ring account is 228487168 bytes = 0.212776 GiB; this is the live Near/SWA ring staging required before skip finalize. It is not misreported as a steady-state saving or hidden by allocator reserved memory.
memory_static_skip.interpretation: Steady savings come from evicting Far on the 13 gated layers, not from direct prefill itself. Direct and conversion have identical final physical storage.

hybrid_memory_and_latency.scope: All rows use no-skip full-linear storage. The small allocated differences are process-level measurements, not main-KV savings.

latency_ms.interpretation: No prefill or TPOT speedup is claimed. The original 128K second-request 85.75s direct prefill outlier is retained; an independent rerun returned to 75.46s with unchanged tokens.

remaining_limits: Strict graph-vs-eager bit-exactness is not universal in the shared decode path: 32K and 128K each have two token differences in both prefill arms. Direct-eager exactly matches conversion-eager, so this does not localize to direct prefill.
The RULER gate is a 16-example direct/conversion equivalence check, not a full quality benchmark and not evidence for arbitrary skip masks.
Chunked/padded/beam/offload/grad prefill, cache geometry changes after finalize, crop/rewind, cache sharing and speculative decoding remain fail-closed or unsupported.
The first-request skip-arm ring staging overhead and all prefill outliers are reported separately from steady-state Far-eviction savings.
